say: Your insight workbook, a report people act on, and your plan.
This is the video for module 4 of Data Literacy.
Your capstone is one Google Sheets file that takes real records from messy to meaningful. Choose data you care about: your sales, your group's contributions, or your orders.

say: In Notes, write your question and a data dictionary: each column's name, meaning, type and allowed values. It lets someone else check your work without asking you.
Do not invent records. The point is to practise on real, imperfect data.

say: Ngozi asks: is my business growing, and why are some customers unhappy? She removes 2 duplicate orders and fills missing delivery dates from her chats.

card.title: Ngozi's three-month workbook
card.note: Revenue by month, from SUMIF and COUNTIF.

say: Revenue grows every month: about 23.8% from July to August, and about 21.2% to September.

card.title: Ngozi's three-month workbook
card.note: Revenue by month, from SUMIF and COUNTIF.

say: In total, 785,000 naira. But COUNTIF shows 10 late orders out of 84, and 8 of the 10 were group aso ebi orders.
Her recommendation: quote group orders a longer time, take deposits earlier, and check whether lateness falls below 5% next quarter.

card.title: Ngozi's three-month workbook

say: Write no more than three findings, each with a number, and name what the data cannot show. Ngozi's data cannot show whether customers left because of lateness, so she plans to ask.
Then run these six checks before you submit.

panel.heading: Accuracy and privacy checks
items: Cleaned rows and total explained in the log
Category totals add up to the overall total
Shares of a whole add up to 100%
Charts have titles, units, and zero axes
Codes, not names or phone numbers
Every column explained in the dictionary

say: A busy manager or donor will not read your spreadsheet. Start with the answer: we asked why deliveries were late, and the main reason is group orders.

panel.heading: The one-page report structure
items: Main message in one sentence
Two or three supporting numbers
One clear chart
What it means
What we should do
panel.rule: Lead with the answer, not the order you did the work.

say: For example, a community programme in Ilorin trained women in bookkeeping. Outputs are what you delivered: 38 of 45 completed.

cards.d: What you delivered: 45 enrolled, 38 completed, about 84.4%.
What changed: 25 of 38 keep weekly sales records, about 65.8%.
7 did not finish because of market days. So she asks to fund a Saturday cohort.

say: Outcomes are what changed. A phone follow-up three months later reached all 38, and 25 now keep weekly records. The donor headline: two in three graduates now keep weekly sales records.

What changed: 25 of 38 keep weekly sales records, about 65.8%.

say: She also reports the 7 who did not finish, and why. Funders usually notice missing numbers, and admitting limits increases trust.
For members, she sends one short WhatsApp message with the same facts and a clear next step.

say: Grow my business cannot be checked. A target names the metric, the starting point, the goal and the date.

For example, Halima's kiosk earns about 95,000 naira a week at a 24% gross margin. In 90 days she will record every sale, raise margin to 26%, measure repeat customers, and test one change, such as a bulk-buy discount for two weeks.
Keep it to about three targets, and spend 30 minutes each week on your records and dashboard.

To remember. Build your workbook from real records. Lead with the answer. Report honestly. To earn your certificate, complete the capstone and score at least 70% in the final quiz. That is 9 of 12 questions.

panel.heading: Remember
items: Five sheets: Raw, Clean, Summary, Charts, Notes
Up to three findings, each with a number
Lead with the answer, then evidence, then action
Report outputs, outcomes and honest gaps
Certificate: capstone plus 9 of 12 in the quiz
